analysis:
This batch contains only documentation changes: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/large-memory-checkpoint-stage-cap.md) and an edit to docs/reference/configuration.md (the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB/_MS row, about line 508 on the head side, plus the date bump). No source code is included, so the actual SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift change that raises the complete-checkpoint staging cap to 7 GiB / 15 s on Macs with at least 96 GiB was not reviewed.

Security relevance is to T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TB-007). The docs state that the daily write cap is unchanged. They also state that the cache's default TTL, encryption and HMAC lookup keys are unchanged and that explicit environment overrides still win. The overrides are not forwarded to LaunchAgents, so installed daemons use the new large-memory defaults.

The next pass should check the code behind these claims:
- The larger staging reservation (up to 7 GiB transient RAM) still goes through GlobalKVCacheBudget and the memory admission checks, with no permanent carve and fail-closed refusal.
- The 15 s time cap is an estimated-read cap, not a deadline that can stall serving (T-010 and T-029 availability).
- The at-rest posture (AES-GCM, K_lookup HMAC, 30-minute TTL, disk budget, write cap) is untouched.
- Deeper restorable prefixes widen the same-account TTFT oracle only in degree (SEC-035, accepted), with no change in kind.

Nothing in the documents changes a security boundary or invalidates a threat assumption.
